### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**45** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4143e31d3a64f0f231ced9268b49880deb6c159a` — the merge of head `9cfc766723c1e79bd24fb924e14a57e3f227470b` into base `41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4143e31d3a64f0f231ced9268b49880deb6c159a && git checkout 4143e31d3a64f0f231ced9268b49880deb6c159a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb 9cfc766723c1e79bd24fb924e14a57e3f227470b && git checkout -B drift-repro 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb && git merge --no-ff 9cfc766723c1e79bd24fb924e14a57e3f227470b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `16a1d37e1df7cb62b01096281a9e5fbf87c0c1ae`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts + packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, content/docs/references/data/data-engine.mdx, .changeset/30237-recycle-bin-purge-empty-permanent.md, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/capture.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/write-epoch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-operation-vocabulary.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/write-epoch.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-delete-dispatch.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/verify/src/handle.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs, docs/adr/0148-recycle-bin-separate-store-restore-under-original-ids-retention-in-days.md

Inputs read: PR #30990 body and file list (13 files, +852/-48); commits 2302a5f0 (spec, 3 files), aa8b43fa (engine), 16a1d37e (merge of origin/main 1aeeafd9); card #30237 body and all 12 comments (one page); the head's check-runs. The read-only shape held: nothing was built, run or re-run. `git merge-tree` was used as a read of git objects to reproduce the merge; `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 30990` and `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` were used as read-only tooling.

### ① Derived judgments

**Scope against the slice and the claim.**

- Confirmed. Every hunk is in PR 2's slice (purge, empty, permanent delete) or is the test and vocabulary work that slice forces. Nothing of PR 3 (restore), PR 4 (`permission.zod.ts`, `OPERATION_TO_PERMISSION`, `GRANT_BITS`) or PR 5 (REST doors) rides along: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/**`, `packages/core/**`, `packages/rest/**` are untouched (file list).
- Confirmed. The spec change is exactly the consented key: `packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts:447-457` adds `permanent: z.boolean().optional()` with a describe, nothing else. Consent 6688058790 covers this key in `data-engine.zod.ts` only, and `permission.zod.ts` is not touched.
- Confirmed. The regenerated shard is exactly what the key implies: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` gains one row, `"data/EngineDeleteOptions:permanent"`, between `:multi` and `:where`; the mdx gains one table row at `content/docs/references/data/data-engine.mdx:659`. The other spec artefacts (`api-surface/data.json`, `declaration-map`, `json-schema.manifest`, `export-origins`, `authorable-defaults`) list export names or defaulted keys, not every key, so they owe no row; `authorable-surface.base.json` is the frozen baseline the ratchet compares against, not a regenerated file.
- Confirmed. All hunks sit inside the claim's file surface (6673233448: `packages/objectql/src/**`; `packages/spec/**` as consented). But the card carries no PR 2 amendment: 6673429400 admits PR 1 only and says "each later PR gets its own amendment"; 6675653517 widens PR 1; 6678640327 lists PR 2 as pending. See ③.

**The merge commit 16a1d37e.**

- Confirmed. `git merge-tree --write-tree aa8b43fa 1aeeafd9` reproduces the merge with one unmerged path, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, which the generated-file merge driver refuses to text-merge. The merge commit's tree differs from that auto-merge tree in that one file only (2 lines). Against the main parent, the merge commit's `data.json` differs by exactly the one `permanent` row, so the regeneration is consistent with main plus the key. No hand edit beyond that resolution.

**Security.**

- Confirmed: `permanent: true` is authorized as `purge`. `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:9153` reads it before the operation context is built; `engine.ts:9160` sets `operation: permanent ? 'purge' : 'delete'`. The check is the chain's: `plugin-security`'s object gate hands the raw verb to `checkObjectPermission` (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:844-849`); `permission-evaluator.ts:305-311` finds no mapping for `purge` and the `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS` set (`:93`) answers deny. So every non-system principal is refused until PR 4 maps the verb to `manageRecycleBin`. Fail-closed, as the body says.
- Confirmed: a caller cannot reach a permanent delete through a batch or by-filter path. `readPermanentDelete` (`purge.ts:115-124`) refuses `permanent: true` unless the dispatch kind is `by-id` and `multi` is not `true`; `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch` (`engine-delete-dispatch.ts:189-219`) is the same ladder the engine routes on. A by-filter delete never dispatches as `purge`.
- Confirmed: no snapshot. `engine.ts:9572` passes `options?.multi === true || permanent` as `skip`, and `capture.ts:332` returns no capture when `skip` is true.
- Confirmed: platform objects are refused for all three acts. `purge.ts:125` and `:192` refuse through `recycleBinTakesObject` (`capture.ts:72-73`, `hasPlatformObjectPrefix` over `sys_`, `cloud_`, `ai_`, `platform-object-names.ts:199`). `purge()` takes its object from the entry's `object_name`, which the bin only ever holds for business objects (Q7, 6675653517).
- Confirmed: the system bypass. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:418` lets `isSystem` through for every verb; that is the existing boundary and the PR names it. The flow-run and app-automation exception (`:404-415`) covers the four identity objects only; a `purge` on a `sys_*` object is refused by the engine first.
- Confirmed: tenant wall for the normal case. `purge()` reads the entry with `buildDriverOptions(RECYCLE_BIN_OBJECT, context)` (`purge.ts:155-159`), so an organization-scoped caller cannot see another organization's entry (test `purge.test.ts:289-298`). `empty()` deletes with the same scope (`purge.ts:198-201`; test `:330-340`). The system is unscoped by design (`:342-348`).
- Should-fix (security, rule level), owed before PR 4 maps the verb: the two object-level `purge` dispatches do not carry the chain's recorded tenant verdict, and the engine's own fallback falls open for a caller with no active organization. `purge.ts:158` and `:198` build the bin's driver options without `recordedVerdict: opCtx.tenantLayer0Verdict`, unlike every engine executor (`engine.ts:4611`, `:9519`, `:7623`). For a `deny` verdict with no active organization, `driverReadScope` answers "no scope" (`engine-driver-options.ts:440-441`), and under `isolated` a caller with no active organization is `deny` (`tenant-layer0-verdict.ts:181`). The chain enforces `deny` through the composed RLS filter on the AST path and the by-id pre-image (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1058-1066`, `:2354-2411`); `purge()` and `empty()` carry neither an AST nor an id, so neither applies. Today the `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS` backstop refuses the dispatch before the executor runs, so nothing is removed, and `purge()`'s pre-dispatch read discloses only whether an entry id exists (403 against `false`). Once PR 4 maps `purge`, an organization-less principal that still clears the object gate would empty every organization's entries of the object. Close it in PR 4's slice or a delta here: refuse (or answer `false` / `0`) when the engine's own Layer-0 verdict is `deny`, and pass the recorded verdict inside the executor.
- Should-fix (boundary), for the seat's judgment: the sandbox body runner forwards a body's own `opts` to `ql.delete` (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts:1133`), and a job body runs under a fresh `{ isSystem: true, tenantId }` envelope (`:1424`). So app-authored job code can now pass `permanent: true` and erase a record with no bin entry, as the system, with no `manageRecycleBin` check. Before this PR the same body's delete entered the bin. The flow delete node cannot (`crud-nodes.ts:1002` builds `{ where, multi, context }`; `DeleteRecordConfigSchema` is a strict object, `builtin-node-config.zod.ts`). The REST and action paths build fixed options (`batch-routes.ts:430`, `action-execution.ts:790`, `:3504`). Whether app-automation's system envelope should stop short of `purge` the way it stops short of identity writes (#25251, #25653) is a maintainer question; it is not a defect of this slice.
- Confirmed, knowingly deferred: a purge or an empty writes no audit row. `plugin-audit` skips `sys_recycle_bin` (`audit-writers.ts:256+`, the PR 1 must-fix A entry) and `purge` names no hook pair (`engine-top-level.ts:165`). The permanent delete is audited through its `afterDelete`. ADR-0148 D3 puts "delete and restore audit reports" on a cloud card, so no open-source ledger row is owed here; the PR body's acceptance note says so.

**Refusals (code, status, message).**

- Confirmed. Every new refusal is `400` with `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` and a `param` (`purge.ts:65-74`): `permanent` not a boolean (`:107-114`); `permanent: true` off the by-id path or with `multi: true` (`:115-124`); `permanent: true` on a platform object (`:125`, `param: 'permanent'`); a bad `entryId` (`:144-151`, `param: 'entryId'`); `empty('')` or a platform object (`:184-192`, `param: 'object'`). Messages name the rule and the fix; `developerMessage` names the object. `VALIDATION_ERROR` is a standard ledger code; no new code is introduced, so `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` owes nothing.
- Confirmed. These are the "permanent-delete refusals" the body calls an accepted deviation. The code matches the body's list exactly: by-filter, `multi: true`, platform prefix, non-boolean. The acceptance itself has no record on the card or the PR. See ③.

**Tests and ablations.**

- Confirmed. `purge.test.ts` runs a real `ObjectQL` under `isolated` with a driver that keeps rows and honours `tenantId` (`:21-91`, `:125-148`). It covers the permanent delete (record and cascade gone, no entry, one `purge` dispatch with id and no AST, hooks see `permanent: true`, `permanent: false` still captures, refusal under a middleware that refuses non-system `purge`, the four 400s), `purge()` (one dispatch with no id, another organization's entry answers `false`, unknown id, no bin, refusal versus system, bad ids) and `empty()` (own organization only, system takes all, pages of 500 on a driver with no `deleteMany`, 1,100 entries in 3 pages, a stuck page ends the loop, unregistered object, refusal, no bin, three 400s).
- Confirmed. The eight ablations in the body would go red as stated, read against the assertions: capture not skipped → `:194`; verb always `delete` → `:196`, `:233` plus the vocabulary pins (`engine-middleware-operation-vocabulary.test.ts:348`, `:362-366`, `:414-421`); refusal only on `reject` → `:243-254` and `:372-384` of the vocabulary file; platform refusal dropped → `:256-264`; entry read unscoped → `:289-298`; `empty` outside the chain → `:339`, `:395`; fallback stops after one page → `:370`; stuck-page guard dropped → `:374-379` never returns. The exact red counts are the dev's; the direction holds.
- Confirmed. The #7809 pin is re-pinned, not loosened: the union is read from the engine source (`:329`), `purge` is the only destructive member (`:340`), every `purge` dispatch is asserted AST-free (`:362-366`), and the AST-carrying set is unchanged (`:410`). The #17713 lifecycle namespace stays at 14 names (`engine-hook-event-dispatch-gap.test.ts:122`) because `ENGINE_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_EVENTS` filters on the verb's boolean (`engine-top-level.ts:174`).

**Census.**

- Confirmed. The tenant-audit census enumerates `packages/services` and `packages/plugins` only (`scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs:248`, `SURFACE_ROOTS`). The raw bin reads and removals in `packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.ts` are outside its population, as `capture.ts`'s raw insert was in PR 1. No census row is owed.

**Check-runs on the head** (last read 2026-11-06 16:13Z): 62 check-runs; 28 success, 8 skipped, 26 in progress (Test Core 1-5, 7, 8; Test UI 1-16; Type Check UI; Type Check workspace; Build Core). None red at either read (16:10Z, 16:13Z). The commit status API reports no statuses. The PR is a draft. Landing waits for all green (contract-review.md ②).

### ② Semver level

Confirmed. `.changeset/30237-recycle-bin-purge-empty-permanent.md` declares `'@objectstack/objectql': minor` and `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` line-initial, matching the PR body. `Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves; both packages that move are listed. The spec adds an optional key with no default and changes no existing behaviour, so it is a widening. In objectql, `OperationContext.operation` gains a member, `WRITE_EPOCH_OPERATIONS` gains `purge`, two engine methods and one type export are added, and `ENGINE_OPERATION_VERBS` changes its value type from `true` to `boolean` (a module-private constant, not exported). No narrowing is hidden: a delete that succeeded before still succeeds, since `permanent` was unreadable before this PR (`engine-unknown-option` refused it as an unknown key), and `beforePurge`/`afterPurge` registration keeps warning rather than refusing (`engine-top-level.ts:160-165`). The changeset body's middleware-author paragraph states the `'purge'` verb and its no-AST rule.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside login to name.
- The dev's PR body and os-dev report (6689274673) say the seat accepted two deviations at 07:31Z: `empty` requires the object, and the permanent-delete refusals. No card comment, PR comment or claim amendment records that acceptance. In the card thread the dev's 07:30Z message asked the seat to look at two trade-offs: `empty` must name the object, and `beforePurge`/`afterPurge` stay warnings. The refusals were in the attached body draft. The seat should record its acceptance of all three (the object parameter, the refusals, the hook namespace) in the PR 2 claim amendment, and confirm it meant the refusals.
- Owed by the seat before landing: the PR 2 claim amendment that 6673429400 promised ("each later PR gets its own amendment"), naming PR 2's file surface (the 13 paths above) and the deviations. The diff is inside the claim's broad surface and the spec consent, so this is a record the seat writes, not a change the dev makes.
- The two should-fix items in ① are flagged for PR 4: the tenant-verdict gap in the object-level `purge` dispatches must be closed before `purge` is mapped to a grant, and the job-body `permanent` door under the system envelope wants a maintainer's word. Neither is reachable by a non-system principal on this head.
- `open_questions` in the os-dev report: none. Out-of-scope finding carried by the seat: the plugin-security sites keyed on `'delete'` (listed in the body under "For PR 4") and `verify`'s `observeWrites` (`packages/verify/src/handle.ts:598`, which records a permanent delete as nothing). Both are correctly left to PR 4.
- Skills-docs: `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md:268`, `:417` still teach that there is no recycle bin; the follow-up is #30847 and the changeset carries the `Skills-docs:` line.
- Governed paths: `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 30990` reports 0 of 13 paths governed; 900 changed lines, under the 3000-line human-merge threshold. Ordinary queue landing applies once the record is in and CI is green.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts` (the one `hits` file), against the ruling it implements and its first consumer.

- The key implements Q3 = A (6676408264) as ruled: `permanent: true` is the purge door, authorized as `purge`, with no snapshot. The describe and docblock say exactly that and name the by-id-only rule, which the engine enforces (`purge.ts:115-124`). The docblock cites ADR-0148 D3, where the sentence lives ("Permanent delete stays available for privacy erasure and never enters the bin", ADR-0148 `:233-234`, `:252`).
- The first consumer is the engine's `delete()` (`engine.ts:9153`), which reads the key through `readPermanentDelete` and through `ENGINE_DELETE_OPTION_KEYS` (`engine-top-level.ts:331-332`), so the unknown-option drift pin derives the accepted key set from the schema and stays green only because the engine admits the key. The hook input type (`spec/src/data/hook-api.ts`, `hook.zod.ts`) carries it to `beforeDelete`/`afterDelete`, which the test shows reading it.
- The key is optional with no default, so every existing author and caller is unchanged; a `false` is the ordinary delete. A non-boolean is refused rather than coerced, which is the right reading of `z.boolean()` at the engine door.
- One wording gap, not a defect: the describe says "By-id deletes only" but not that `multi: true` beside an id is also refused. The engine says so in its refusal message, and the docblock says it. No change asked.

The spec change holds against the ruling, its consumer and the acceptance scenarios. No must-fix.

## Hold · 2026-11-06T16:52Z · Test Core (2/8) red on `16a1d37e`: a real failure in this PR

`packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.test.ts:232`, drift pin "HookDeleteOptions / EngineDeleteOptionsSchema": `EngineDeleteOptionsSchema` now has `permanent`, and the pin's KEPT ∪ OMITTED (`where`, `multi` / `context`) does not list it. As typed today, `HookDeleteOptions = Omit<EngineDeleteOptions, 'context'>`, so a hook's `ctx.api.object(n).delete()` can pass `permanent: true`.

The fix needs a decision on the published hook face.
